clue.text: Cell entrance is blocked by this writer

indicators.note: the entrance word is blocked, with another piece stopping up its middle

parts.note: a gate is an entrance to a field or yard
the setter refers to themself as ME

explanation.surface: A prison cell door is barred by the person writing this clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cell' suggests a prison, but it is the biological sense: a reproductive cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamete is a reproductive cell, such as a sperm or an egg, that fuses with another in fertilisation.

clue.text: Leaving the wife and making a 50/50 settlement

parts.note: going means leaving
my old Dutch is Cockney slang for one's wife

explanation.surface: A husband walks out and splits everything equally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' is old Cockney slang for a wife (from 'duchess').
explanation.definitionFit: Going Dutch is an idiom for each person paying their own share, splitting a bill equally.

clue.text: Gym's put in up-to date sort of bike

indicators.note: put in places the gym letters inside the word for up-to-date

parts.note: mod is short for modern, up-to-date
PE, physical education, is school gym

explanation.surface: A gym installs a fashionable kind of exercise bike.
explanation.definitionFit: A moped is a light motorbike with pedals, a kind of bike.

clue.text: The deficient sportsman who offends the umpire?

indicators.note: deficient means lacking a part, here the final letter

parts.note: a rower is an oarsman, a sportsman

explanation.surface: A cheat in sport whose lack of skill annoys the official.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a bowler who straightens the arm is 'throwing', an illegal action the umpire calls.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket bowler with an illegal straight-arm action is called for throwing, offending against the umpire's rulings.

clue.text: Soldiers kept in farm building as stock must be

indicators.note: the soldiers are kept inside the farm building, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a stable is a farm building for horses
OR, other ranks, is the usual abbreviation for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops are quartered in a barn, which is how livestock must be housed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' reads as livestock, but here it means goods kept in stock, which must be able to be stored.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods held in stock have to be capable of being kept in a store, so an adjective describing them fits.

clue.text: She is one beloved of crossworders!

definitions.text: She is one beloved of crossworders!

parts.words: She is one beloved of crossworders!
parts.note: She is the novel by H. Rider Haggard, much used by setters to clue a short book name

explanation.surface: A remark about a woman adored by puzzle-solvers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' looks like a woman, but it is Haggard's novel, a favourite of setters.
explanation.definitionFit: She, Haggard's adventure novel, is a book name, which crossword setters often clue that way.

clue.text: Back ruler up with a bit of Scripture

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
a verse is a short numbered section of the Bible

explanation.surface: Support a monarch with a Bible quotation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ER into RE. 'Back' reads as support, but it means rear or opposite side.
explanation.definitionFit: The reverse is the back of a coin or page, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Robber stifles expression of surprise when rat is seen

indicators.note: stifles means smothers, so the robber wraps round the exclamation

parts.note: a bandit is a robber
coo is a British exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A thief keeps quiet about his shock at spotting a rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: The bandicoot rat is a large South Asian rodent, so the name can stand for a kind of rat.

clue.text: Novel with new ending gets award in America

indicators.note: with new ending says the last letter of the novel is swapped for another

parts.note: Emma is a novel by Jane Austen

explanation.surface: A book's revised conclusion wins it a US prize.
explanation.definitionFit: An Emmy is an American television award.

clue.text: Thing under piano may be just a speck of dust

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts the thing below the piano letter

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft
an article is a thing or item

explanation.surface: An object beneath a piano might be nothing more than a fleck of dust.
explanation.definitionFit: A particle is a tiny fragment of matter, and a speck of dust is an example.

clue.text: Damaged armpit not significant

indicators.note: damaged signals that the letters of the following words are knocked out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: An injured armpit is nothing to worry about.
explanation.definitionFit: Something significant matters, which is a straightforward synonym for weighty or consequential.

clue.text: Archdeacon's order conveying malice

parts.note: Ven, for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A senior clergyman issues a command full of spite.
explanation.walkthrough: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour; an archdeacon is styled 'the Venerable'.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom figuratively means spite or bitter hostility, a close synonym of malice.

clue.text: Sink into oblivion, as drips might?

definitions.meaning: to be wasted or lost entirely, an idiom for failure
drips of water literally run down the plughole of a sink

explanation.surface: A double reading: being lost to memory, and water dripping away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sink' in the first sense chimes with the kitchen sink of the second, which is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be wasted or lost for good, and drips literally go down a plughole.

clue.text: Mediocre support leads to rebuke

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it
to rate someone is an old verb for scolding them

explanation.surface: Weak backing ends in a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-rate means of inferior quality, a synonym of mediocre.

clue.text: Effusive person no good as a guide

indicators.note: no here means without, so the letter for good is taken away

parts.note: a gusher is someone who talks with excessive enthusiasm

explanation.surface: Someone over-enthusiastic is useless at showing people round.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher guides people to their seats in a theatre, church or court, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Men woo her, amazingly? She has this property

indicators.note: amazingly signals the letters of the preceding words are thrown into confusion

explanation.surface: Suitors court a woman, astonishingly; she owns a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amazingly' rearranges MEN, WOO and HER together.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has a house of their own as property is its owner-occupier.

clue.text: Hesitation to go with bloke? Then get one!

definitions.text: Hesitation to go with bloke? Then get one!

parts.note: chap is an informal British word for a man or bloke
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Advice to a nervous young woman: if unsure about going out with a man, bring a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR added a stray 'Is'; the page omits it. The whole clue is also the definition: a hesitant young lady would take an escort.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperone is an older companion who accompanies a young unmarried woman on outings with men.

clue.text: I taste an unusual chemical element

indicators.note: unusual signals the preceding letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A taster reports an odd chemical flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Astatine is a radioactive element, number 85, in the halogen group.

clue.text: Food product one of the team brought aboard yacht

indicators.note: brought aboard places one piece inside the vessel named next

parts.note: a cat, short for catamaran, is a sailing yacht with twin hulls
a member is one of a team

explanation.surface: A crew member is welcomed onto a sailing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Camembert is a soft French cheese, an example of a food product.

clue.text: Part of America with gold in glacier deposit

indicators.note: in places the gold letters inside the American state

parts.note: Maine is a US state
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A region of the USA where gold is found in glacial debris.
explanation.definitionFit: A moraine is the ridge of rock and soil deposited by a glacier.

clue.text: Arrive in poor area with hour to spend

indicators.note: to spend means to use up, so the hour letter is lost from the poor area

parts.note: a ghetto is a poor, crowded part of a city

explanation.surface: Someone turns up in a deprived district with an hour to kill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrive in' looks like one phrase; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To get to a place is to arrive there, a phrasal verb with the same meaning.

clue.text: Modern music accepted by British? On the contrary —- it's rubbish!

indicators.note: accepted by would put the music inside the British letter
on the contrary reverses the roles, so British goes inside the music

parts.note: garage is a style of electronic dance music

explanation.surface: Modern pop is welcomed in Britain, or the reverse: it is junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted by' as written would put the music inside B; 'On the contrary' swaps the roles.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage is an American word for rubbish or refuse.

clue.text: This is one unacceptable thing shown by some stars?

definitions.text: This is one unacceptable thing shown by some stars?

parts.words: This is one unacceptable thing shown by some stars?
parts.note: rude words in print are replaced by asterisks, typically four of them; also, the word This itself has four letters

explanation.surface: A remark about objectionable behaviour by celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' suggests celebrities, but it means asterisks, used to blank out swear words.
explanation.definitionFit: A swear word of the classic kind is blanked out in print as a row of asterisks, and the clue's first word itself has four letters.

clue.text: Exclusive twelve pitch in the office

definitions.meaning: select, of the best or most privileged group
a typewriter typeface with twelve characters to the inch

explanation.surface: A select group meets in an office, with a typing reference.
explanation.walkthrough: On typewriters, elite type had twelve characters per inch; pica had ten.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means a select group, and as a typing term the twelve-to-the-inch typewriter face.

clue.text: Bird must get insect, first to last

indicators.note: first to last moves the opening letter of the insect to the end

parts.note: a louse is a small parasitic insect

explanation.surface: A bird has to catch a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: An ousel, or ouzel, is an old name for the blackbird, and the ring ouzel is a thrush.

clue.text: Not the latest in aircraft design

indicators.note: not the latest means without the last letter of the aircraft word

parts.note: a plane is an aircraft

explanation.surface: An outdated aeroplane blueprint.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a design or scheme drawn up in advance.

clue.text: Piece of cloth stuck to one about to fall off

indicators.note: fall off says the letter for about drops away from the word for stuck

parts.note: clung means stuck fast, held on tightly
C, for circa, means about
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A scrap of fabric clings to someone on the point of tumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: A lungi is a cloth wrapped round the waist, worn in South Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A lungi is a length of cloth worn as a sarong in India, Bangladesh and Myanmar.

clue.text: The main attraction of Corfu?

parts.note: main is an old word for the open sea, so this asks which body of water lies round the Greek island

explanation.surface: A tourist question about the best thing on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main attraction' reads as the chief sight, but 'the main' is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu lies in the stretch of the Mediterranean west of Greece, so that water is the island's 'main'.

clue.text: Scandinavians seem excited when goddess comes round

indicators.note: the goddess comes round, enclosing the other letters

parts.note: a Norn is one of the Norse goddesses of fate

indicators.note: excited signals that the letters of seem are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Northern Europeans grow agitated when a deity encircles them.
explanation.walkthrough: The Norns are the three Fates of Norse myth; 'excited' shuffles the four letters the goddess's name then wraps round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norsemen were the people of ancient Scandinavia, notably the Vikings.

clue.text: Breakfast? That is only a bit of cereal

parts.note: breakfast is a meal
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A complaint that the morning meal was just a few flakes.
explanation.walkthrough: Mealie is a South African word for maize, especially a single ear of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mealie is an ear of maize in South African English, so a single piece of a cereal crop.
